scope_note: Third-pass public-evidence and corrective gap-closure audit for the Quicken Loans Technology Center, now marketed as the Rocket Mortgage Technology Center, at 1401 Rosa Parks Boulevard in Detroit, Wayne County, Michigan. The selected account is Quicken/Rocket's partial tenancy and data-center use within a landlord-controlled mixed office and data-center property, not the entire combined parcel, separate personal-property accounts, another tenant, the corporate technology workforce, Bedrock's Detroit portfolio, or later third-party utility work. Four direct quantitative observations remain preserved: the 66,000-square-foot opening footprint, 1.4 MW of completed-facility redundant available power, approximately 70 electricians employed on the project by January 2015, and a $24,044.58 DTE Electric rerouting estimate to be borne by the property petitioner. The authoritative current assessor service traces the 2017 parcel combination to four predecessors, while the live Wayne County search exposes separate real- and personal-property accounts at the address. The recovered May 2018 Legislative Policy Division report inventories 15 Quicken/Bedrock projects and 27 City incentives but omits this technology center. Two low-confidence last-resort syntheses now pass separately: a whole-facility nameplate-to-annual-electricity sensitivity and an electrician-only wage-payroll sensitivity. Neither is observed consumption or payroll. Realized total investment, total construction labor, supplier payments and locality, operating employment and payroll, tax bills and payments, project incentive value, public-service costs, metered resources, emissions, community transfers, and a causal county counterfactual remain unresolved.

sources.title: Construction Underway On New, Detroit-based Quicken Loans Technology Center
sources.notes: The operator says Quicken Loans and Bedrock began construction on May 20, 2014 at 1401 Rosa Parks Boulevard. It describes a 66,000-square-foot office and data-center complex with two 10,000-square-foot server rooms, half occupied by Quicken's technology team and an equal 33,000-square-foot portion available to another tenant. Its 1.4 MW statement was prospective and its 1,100-member IT-team figure was company-wide, so neither is treated here as a contemporaneous operating observation or site employment.

sources.title: Rocket Mortgage Technology Center
sources.notes: Current landlord marketing identifies the property as the Rocket Mortgage Technology Center, classifies it as office and data center, and says it remains partially occupied by the Rocket Mortgage Information Technology team. Its 85,000-RSF figure is not harmonized with the 66,000-square-foot opening description, the SEC lease's 65,250 rentable square feet, or the assessor parcel's six buildings and 68,718 square feet; the incompatible measures are preserved as a boundary discrepancy rather than an added quantitative record.

sources.title: Quicken Loans Data Centers
sources.notes: The electrical contractor identifies the exact address, Quicken Loans and Bedrock as clients, Turner Construction as selector, a 2015 completion, and 1.4 MW of redundant available power. Internet Archive comparison shows the $4.8 million field was absent from snapshots through May 2025 and present after the contractor's late-2025 site redesign. Comparison with the site's other project pages shows the generic Value field can reproduce a whole-project amount rather than the contractor's own package. Because this page does not define the amount as total project cost, paid electrical contract value, local supplier spend, or a Quicken payment, it is not converted into an evidence record.

sources.title: Electricians power Quicken's new technology center
sources.publisher: Michigan Building and Construction Trades Council
sources.notes: The trade publication reports that about 70 IBEW Local 58 electricians had been employed on the project since its spring 2014 groundbreaking, mostly by Motor City Electric, with Turner managing the project and GSI, LaBelle and Madison Heights Glass also identified. It describes two underground DTE feeds, fiber conduit and a pair of 2.5 MW diesel generators for Quicken's DC-1, but supplies no total construction headcount, hours, payroll, worker residence, contract payments or generator runtime.

sources.title: Detroit City Council Proceedings, September 16, 2014 — Petition 146
sources.notes: Printed pages 1913-1914 document Giffels Webster's Petition 146 on behalf of 1401 Rosa Parks Blvd. LLC to vacate alleys and easements in the project block. The adopted resolution reports DTE Electric's $24,044.58 estimate for removing or rerouting services and states that the petitioner must bear that expense; it also places DWSD sewer relocation, survey, engineering and inspection costs on the petitioner without quantifying them. Both relevant PDF pages were rendered and visually inspected.

sources.title: Detroit BSEED Building Permits, 2019-present

sources.notes: An exact query for UPPER(address) LIKE '%1401 ROSA PARKS%' OR parcel_id='08008283-303' returned BLD2019-03107 at 1415 Rosa Parks Boulevard, a $45,000 interior renovation on the later combined parcel. Because its address and work are distinct from the selected 2014-2015 technology-center development, it is excluded rather than assigned through parcel overlap. The current open dataset begins in 2019 and cannot establish absence of the original building permits.

sources.notes: Exact address, Quicken and Bedrock searches located ENG-21-19, issued May 5, 2021 for 123Net underground fiber work reaching the rear of 1401 Rosa Parks, and ENG-26-202, issued May 8, 2026 for Comcast coax and conduit to the address. Both are later no-fee telecommunications right-of-way permits; neither quantifies the 2014-2015 project, a facility payment, network use, or public cost.

sources.title: Wayne County Property Tax Online
sources.notes: The live address search returned real parcel 08008283-303 and separate personal-property accounts at 1401 Rosa Parks, including 08990518.03 for Rocket Mortgage LLC, 08990518.04 for Rocket Close LLC, 08990518.05 for Rock Limited Partnership, and accounts for unrelated occupants. Exact searches also returned predecessor real parcels 08008268-70 at 1415 Rosa Parks, 08008283-5 at 1404 Vermont, 08008286-9 at 1430 Vermont, and 08008290-303 at 1458 Vermont, each under the property entity/Bedrock-related taxpayer names. The portal reported no outstanding delinquent taxes for the exact records inspected but exposed no current-year bill, payment amount, payment date, assessed personal-property value, or jurisdictional distribution. No-delinquency status is not converted to a zero tax or payment claim.

sources.title: Detroit Parcels (Current)
sources.notes: The authoritative current service identifies 08008283-303 as a taxable commercial-improved parcel at 1401 Rosa Parks Boulevard with six buildings, Computer Centers building style, 2015 year built, 68,718 square feet of total floor area and 2.753 acres. Its legal description states that the parcel was split/combined on November 6, 2017 from 08008268-70, 08008283-5, 08008286-9 and 08008290-303. A September 7, 2026 query returned current/prior assessed values of $3,871,600/$3,781,000 and taxable values of $2,978,823/$2,900,510, which conflict with values carried from the deprecated parcel service; no duplicate quantitative claims are appended here. The real-parcel record has no NEZ district or related-parcel ID, but those blank fields do not prove absence of separate personal-property or other exemption accounts.

The current Certificate of Occupancy ArcGIS service likewise returned no target record for the current or four predecessor parcel IDs, address range, Quicken, or Technology Center. project_updates.title: Project boundary and operator chronology fixed before measurement
project_updates.notes: Direct discovery and gap closure searched Rocket/Quicken and Bedrock current pages, archived releases, Rocket history, SEC exhibits and exact web/archive terms for Quicken Loans Technology Center, Rocket Mortgage Technology Center, 1401 Rosa Parks, 1401 Rosa Parks Blvd. LLC, Ward 08 Items 8268-70 and 8286-9, and parcel 08008283-303 across 2013-2026. Material records opened were the May 20, 2014 construction release, June 30, 2015 opening release, January 19, 2015 SEC-filed lease and current Bedrock property page. The boundary is Quicken/Rocket's partial tenancy and data-center function inside a landlord-controlled mixed-use building: construction began May 20, 2014, the lease commenced January 19, 2015, and the grand opening occurred June 30, 2015. The current Bedrock 85,000-RSF figure conflicts with the opening, lease and assessor definitions, so it is not added or used to rescale evidence. Company-wide IT-team figures and other tenants remain outside scope.
project_updates.project_description: The Quicken Loans Technology Center, now marketed as the Rocket Mortgage Technology Center, is a mixed office and data-center building at 1401 Rosa Parks Boulevard in Detroit's Corktown neighborhood. Quicken Loans and Bedrock began construction in May 2014, Quicken's lease commenced January 19, 2015, and the company held the grand opening on June 30, 2015. The opening materials describe a 66,000-square-foot complex with two 10,000-square-foot server rooms, while Quicken's lease covers 35,920 rentable square feet; this account therefore separates Quicken/Rocket's partial tenancy and data-center function from the landlord's larger property, combined parcel, later work, and other tenants.

project_updates.title: Parcel, personal-property, bill, payment and exemption gap closure
project_updates.notes: The authoritative Detroit service resolves taxable commercial-improved parcel 08008283-303 and traces its November 6, 2017 combination to four predecessors: 08008268-70 at 1415 Rosa Parks, 08008283-5 at 1404 Vermont, 08008286-9 at 1430 Vermont and 08008290-303 at 1458 Vermont. Wayne County's live address search independently returns those real accounts and separately exposes personal-property accounts for Rocket Mortgage LLC (08990518.03), Rocket Close LLC (08990518.04), Rock Limited Partnership (08990518.05), and other occupants. The personal accounts cannot be collapsed into the landlord's real parcel or allocated to the data-center function. The city service's September 7, 2026 current/prior assessed values ($3,871,600/$3,781,000) and taxable values ($2,978,823/$2,900,510) conflict with the deprecated service values already carried in base evidence, so this append-only project fragment records the correction trail without creating duplicate same-period claims. The Wayne records inspected reported no outstanding delinquent taxes but exposed no current bill or payment amount. Michigan Treasury PA 198 and exact exemption searches produced no target certificate. Bills, payments, assessed personal property and project-specific exemptions therefore remain unknown rather than zero.

project_updates.title: Development, incentive, financing and public-cost search remains non-quantified
project_updates.notes: The May 21, 2018 Legislative Policy Division report was recovered through the Internet Archive and its full 11-page project inventory was visually checked. It lists 15 Quicken-family projects and 27 requested or received City incentives across OPRA, PA 210, PA 328, brownfield, PA 147 NEZ and PILOT programs. The 1401 Rosa Parks Technology Center, its property LLC and parcel are absent. The report's family-wide abatements and captured-tax totals belong to the named portfolio projects and are not allocated here. Parallel 2013-2026 searches covered DBRA and DEGC project/board materials, City budgets and ACFRs, Michigan MEDC/Michigan Business records, Michigan Treasury abatements, and exact target terms with incentive, abatement, PILOT, bond, TIF, IRB, grant, compliance, clawback, audit, agenda, attachment, check register and payment. No target-specific development agreement, brownfield plan, certificate, bond, PILOT, TIF, grant, compliance report, payment or quantified public-service cost was located. The LPD omission materially narrows the City incentive trail but does not prove that no aid existed outside its coverage.

project_updates.title: Planning and permit audit preserves one bounded utility projection
project_updates.notes: Permit and land-use searches covered Detroit BSEED's live Accela/eLAPS search, Building, Trades and Certificate of Occupancy ArcGIS services, historical Detroit open-data references, City Council proceedings and City Planning Commission materials. The live portal was searched for January 1, 2013 through December 31, 2016 at 1401 Rosa Parks Boulevard, across 1400-1500 Rosa Parks, and by project name Quicken; it returned no records. The occupancy service returned no target record for the current or four predecessor parcel IDs, address range, Quicken, or Technology Center. Those bounded current-system non-results cannot establish original permit absence. BLD2019-03107 at 1415 is excluded as separate later interior work; ELE2019-03832 is later and valueless. The 2014 council resolution verifies alley/easement action and the $24,044.58 DTE estimate borne by the petitioner, while unpriced DWSD work remains a gap. The 2026 CPC presentation says Detroit zoning does not specifically address data centers; it is not the project's approval.

project_updates.title: Utility, resource and public-infrastructure searches stop at capacity
project_updates.notes: Sources checked for 2013-2026 were Detroit right-of-way permits, DTE Energy and Michigan Public Service Commission dockets/tariffs, Detroit Water and Sewerage Department rates and records, council utility clearances, operator and contractor facility descriptions, and exact address/entity searches for electric, gas, water, wastewater, reclaimed water, transmission, substation, tariff, meter, peak, bill, fiber and generator. The contractor supports 1.4 MW of redundant available power; the trade report identifies two DTE feeds, two 2.5 MW generators for DC-1 and construction-era fiber conduit. Later no-fee permits ENG-21-19 and ENG-26-202 concern 123Net and Comcast work and are not assigned to original project cost or benefit. No facility meter, annual kWh, peak demand, electricity bill, gas use, total water, wastewater, reclaimed-water use, generator runtime, tariff arrangement, transmission/substation allocation or realized public-infrastructure cost was found. The cooling-design claim cannot establish zero total water.

project_updates.title: Environmental and operating-permit gap remains address-history sensitive
project_updates.notes: The corrective search covered Michigan EGLE facility, Part 201, UST/LUST, air and environmental indexes; EPA ECHO/RCRA indexed results; Detroit BSEED environmental and operating-permit materials; and exact searches for 1401 Rosa Parks Boulevard, the common OCR error 1401 Rosa Barks, facility identifiers 00036222 and 82006956, Quicken, Rocket, Bedrock, generator, diesel, air permit, emissions and discharge over 1990-2026. Search results surfaced 1401 in third-party EDR tables embedded in environmental assessments for other Detroit properties, including legacy trucking/warehouse-era listings, but no primary record linked those entries to the 2014-2015 data-center operator or current parcel boundary. The records are excluded rather than inherited across address history. No attributable operating permit, generator fuel/runtime, actual emissions, spill, discharge, penalty or quantified externality was located; blocked or index-only access cannot prove absence.

project_updates.title: Workforce search adds an electrician subset, not total labor
project_updates.notes: Workforce sources checked for 2013-2026 included Rocket/Quicken releases and careers, SEC filings, Michigan Building Trades and IBEW materials, Turner and contractor pages, Michigan workforce/apprenticeship resources, BLS OEWS/QCEW and exact address/project searches for employees, jobs, headcount, payroll, wages, occupation, residence, training, apprenticeship, union and hiring. The January 9, 2015 trade report supports about 70 electricians employed on the project since the May 20, 2014 groundbreaking, mostly through Motor City Electric. The exact dates define a 234-day elapsed interval; BLS reports a May 2016 Detroit-Warren-Dearborn mean electrician wage of $29.16 per hour. Those inputs support only a low-confidence electrician wage-payroll duration sensitivity, not observed payroll, total construction labor, benefits or local household income. Operator references to 1,100- and 1,400-member technology teams are company-wide and excluded. No total construction workforce, actual hours, certified payroll, worker residence, full occupation mix, apprenticeship count, operating FTE, site payroll, turnover or training payment was found.

project_updates.title: Contractor and supplier matrix identifies participants but no payments
project_updates.notes: The supplier/procurement pass searched 2013-2026 operator, Bedrock, Turner, Motor City Electric, Integrated Design Solutions, Giffels Webster, IBEW/trade, City procurement, agenda and check-register materials using the exact project/address plus contractor, subcontractor, vendor, procurement, bid, contract, payment, certified payroll and local spend. Sources identify Turner as construction manager; Motor City Electric, GSI and LaBelle as electrical contractors; Madison Heights Glass; Giffels Webster for the right-of-way petition; and dPop for office design. Internet Archive snapshots show that MCE's generic $4.8 million Value field was added only after a late-2025 site redesign. Cross-page comparison shows the same field can reproduce an entire client's project value, so it cannot be assumed to be MCE's contract or paid amount. No invoice, payment ledger, full subcontract roster, vendor location at payment time, local-purchase share or certified payroll was found. The $4.8 million remains contextual rather than a supplier, investment or local-spend record.

project_updates.title: Community and recipient-side searches find no site-attributable transfer
project_updates.notes: Community searches covered Rocket Community Fund and Rocket Companies social-impact materials, Detroit City Council and neighborhood sources, Detroit PAL and other indexed recipient sites, and exact combinations of Quicken Loans Technology Center, Rocket Mortgage Technology Center, 1401 Rosa Parks and Corktown with grant, donation, sponsorship, nonprofit, school, workforce program, training and community benefit for 2013-2026. Results described company-wide or city-wide Rocket/Quicken initiatives such as housing and connectivity programs but did not identify a cash or in-kind transfer from this facility, a recipient-confirmed 1401 award, a community-benefit agreement, annual site contribution or project-funded training amount. Corporate philanthropy is not allocated by address, tenancy or floor area. The non-result is an attribution gap, not evidence that no community activity occurred.

project_updates.title: Archives, structured data, local reporting and filings cross-check the boundary
project_updates.notes: Cross-source gap closure used Rocket and Bedrock web archives/current pages; SEC EDGAR lease exhibits and subsequent Rocket annual-report exhibit indexes; Detroit ArcGIS parcel, permit and right-of-way services; City Council 2014 and 2018 proceedings; Michigan agency indexes; and local trade and construction reporting for 2013-2026. The lease gives 35,920 rentable square feet, 55.05% tenant share and a January 31, 2030 expiration but redacts rent. Structured data tie later parcel and permit activity to the address while exposing boundary changes; local reporting supplies trade labor and supplier names but not payments. A reported 2013 property acquisition is excluded because it predates development, covers the landlord's real estate and lacks a project-cost crosswalk. Federal/state filings did not yield facility revenue, operating expense, employment, utility use or project-specific aid.

project_updates.title: Candidate-by-candidate modeling review retains two bounded sensitivities
project_updates.notes: Every residual candidate was re-evaluated after third-pass gap closure. Resources: retain a low-confidence whole-facility annual electricity-throughput sensitivity of 3.066-12.264 million kWh using 25%, 50% and 100% of the reported 1.4 MW available-power nameplate; the high endpoint is a mathematical ceiling, not a prediction, and no PUE, cost or emissions factor is applied. Construction: retain a low-confidence electrician-only wage-payroll sensitivity of $682,344-$2,729,376 using about 70 electricians, the 234-day groundbreaking-to-report interval, a 40-hour week, BLS's $29.16 near-period area mean wage, and 25%, 50% and 100% duration shares. It excludes other trades, benefits, overtime and residence effects. Investment: reject; the MCE $4.8 million label, predevelopment property sale and $24,044.58 utility estimate have incompatible scopes and no final capital ledger. Suppliers: reject; named firms lack payments and locality. Operations/minimum coverage: reject; no source requires even one continuously staffed on-site position. Fiscal/public costs: reject; separate real and personal accounts still lack same-scope bills, payments, recipient revenue, project incentive value and marginal service cost. Community: reject; no project-specific recipient amount exists. County effects: reject; Wayne County aggregates lack facility linkage and a credible counterfactual. No lease-share allocation, PUE transfer, electricity-price or emissions extension, supplier multiplier, fiscal break-even, operating staffing model, community proxy or county causal claim is retained.
